text:
Florida arrives on a 4-1-0 run, fresh off a 5-3 win over Chicago, but it is doing this without Brad Marchand (knee) and Aleksander Barkov (knee), both on injured reserve. Carter Verhaeghe has moved onto the line with Sam Reinhart and Brady Tkachuk, and Lars Eller is up to 16:58 a night. Washington is 3-2-0 in its last five and coming off a 6-5 loss to Dallas, in which Jason Robertson scored three goals. The Capitals are also without Vincent Desharnais.

Our numbers see little separating them. At five on five, Florida has taken 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and Washington 53%, and our model projects 3.38 goals for Washington and 3.22 for Florida. The special-teams matchup to watch is Florida's power play, which creates 1.14 expected goals a game, against a Washington penalty kill that allows 0.80. Florida also takes 5.2 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Jacob Markstrom (-0.57 goals saved above expected this season, -15.98 last) and Logan Thompson (+1.23 this season, +28.16 last) point toward Washington.

Verhaeghe is on a five-game point streak and has 13 points in his last ten. We give him a 32% chance to score. Reinhart has goals in four straight, with a 39% chance tonight, and Tkachuk has 16 points in ten. For Washington, Alex Tuch has the highest goal probability in the game at 39%. Tom Wilson has no points in his last ten despite 3.4 expected goals, and we put him at 29%, a player due for one to go in.
